name: gstack
works_with: Claude Code in full. Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and others as experimental. This skill also covers Capy
short: Sets up gstack, Garry Tan's set of slash commands for planning, review, QA, security and shipping, and checks the install works.
what: gstack turns a coding agent into a set of specialist roles, from product review to code review, browser QA, security audits and release. This skill is the gstack entry for Capy and Claude Code: at session start it runs an install check, installs gstack only when a workflow needs it, and then loads the right workflow file. The README says it is all slash commands and Markdown.
who: Founders, tech leads and first-time coding agent users who want structured roles instead of a blank prompt. Skip it if you want something small: it is a large toolkit with hooks, a bundled browser and an update check.
needs: Claude Code, or another supported agent
Bun v1.4.2+ (setup refuses Bun older than 1.3.3)
Node.js on Windows, where it works through Git Bash or WSL

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: The README has you paste an install request into Claude Code, which runs this command and adds a short gstack section to CLAUDE.md.

steps.title: Or install for other agents
steps.text: `--host auto` installs for every agent setup finds on the machine.
steps.code:
git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/garrytan/gstack.git ~/gstack
cd ~/gstack && ./setup --host auto      # or: ./setup --host codex
./setup --status                         # one row per install: host, tier, scope, version, path

steps.title: Start with office hours
steps.text: Run `/office-hours` and describe what you are building. It writes a design doc the other skills read.

steps.title: Review and test
steps.text: Run `/review` on a branch with changes, then `/qa` on your staging URL. When you want the whole sprint, `/autoplan` and `/ship` take over.

steps.title: Check the install
steps.text: The doctor prints one row per check with the fix for anything that fails.

try.label: From the README
try.text: /office-hours, then describe what you are building.

watch: Setup registers hooks and builds a bundled browser, and the browser skills on macOS can use your real logged-in sessions in the Aside browser.
The update check is on by default and makes a few GitHub requests. Turn it off with `gstack-config set update_check false`.
Outside reviews are on by default and send code to Codex or Claude Code under your own login. Turn them off with `gstack-config set codex_reviews disabled`.
Telemetry is off by default and asked about once.
The skill's own installer targets Capy's Ubuntu cloud machines and says not to run it on a personal device without permission.
Team mode commits a gstack requirement into your repo, and its `required` hook needs Node.js for every teammate.
